nina_cs: FYI NovaEdge onboarding, Python FastAPI on GCF. They see a burst of 429s when a new revision scales from 0->10. Pattern: every new container does a preflight auth + immediate request fanout. Happens only for first ~20s. Any quick fixes?

leo_eng: Classic preflight/concurrency stampede. Which SDK and auth flow?

nina_cs: Using python-sdk 0.7.1, custom ephemeral token endpoint that mints per-container JWTs.

todd_sre: Two parallel approaches: client mitigations and short-term ops. Client: add a tiny startup hold + single-flight token fetch per container. In Python use file-lock on /tmp/redwood_token to coordinate processes: if token file exists and not expired, reuse; otherwise acquire lock and fetch. Also enable REDWOOD_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 in env for warmup runs.

leo_eng: Also recommend TCP keepalive + connection pooling so warmup doesn't create new TLS handshakes for each request; fewer connections reduces preflight hits. For FastAPI/gunicorn, use a single background token refresher that seeds container memory and refreshes every N seconds.

nina_cs: Can you paste a small snippet for the SRE?

leo_eng: Send this: "Mitigation steps: (1) upgrade python-sdk to 0.7.3+; (2) implement a /tmp token cache with a simple file-lock single-flight; (3) set REDWOOD_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 for deploy warmups; (4) add randomized init delay (0-250ms) as a last resort; (5) enable keepalive/pool settings in HTTP client to reuse connections. Example single-flight pattern: 

```
import fcntl
import os
import time
TOKEN_PATH='/tmp/redwood_token'
with open(TOKEN_PATH, 'a+') as f:
    fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
    f.seek(0)
    data = f.read()
    if valid(data):
        token = data
    else:
        token = fetch_ephemeral()
        f.seek(0)
        f.truncate()
        f.write(token)
    fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
```

This serializes minting per-container and avoids concurrent token creation spikes." 

nina_cs: Customer applied REDWOOD_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 + file-lock caching and saw the 429s drop to near zero. They asked if we can grant a temporary token-minting grace for new accounts during initial ramp.

todd_sre: Ops-side we can offer a short-lived onboarding quota bump for verified new customers for 48 hours; will need CS approval flow. For product-level changes (server-side token backoff), file an RFC.

docs-bot: Created docs draft in onboarding-playbook/serverless-patterns about file-cache + keepalive patterns.

infra-bot: Ticket created CS-10021 to track onboarding quota bump process and SDK upgrade follow-up.

nina_cs: I'll share the doc with NovaEdge and route for a temporary quota bump request. Closing thread unless they report regression. Thanks all.
